haiku-low.q1: MySQL transaction changes users and inserts outbox row, then commits; then inline copy to Postgres (200 ms timeout, circuit breaker). Postgres failure never fails the request; caller sees success.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the stored row's version is lower than the incoming version, and the id has no tombstone. Otherwise the copy is skipped or ignored.
haiku-low.q3: Phase 0.3: every web and worker instance runs the new build and reports users_write_state. Phase 1.2: all report mysql for at least 60 s. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: Batches of at most 2,000 rows read from the replica. It pauses 2 s when replica lag is missing or above 5 s, and holds a 60 s lease.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: latest compare pass clean within 24 h, ramp 1/10/50/100%. Source of truth: at least 72 h at 100% reads, writes paused, outbox drained, id counter set, checks pass.
haiku-low.q6: The users_outbox row in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the change. The repair worker retries with backoff, copies the current primary row to Postgres, then deletes the outbox row.
haiku-low.q7: Copies skip ids with a tombstone, but the doc admits a brief window where an erased user can reappear before the delete reaches Postgres. This is an open question, not yet decided.
haiku-low.q8: In users_migration_state in Postgres: last_id, lease owner and expiry. Rows and checkpoint commit in one transaction. It stops when a batch comes back empty.
haiku-low.q9: The compare pass scans both tables in id order and flags differences, including Postgres-only ids. It re-reads the MySQL primary; confirmed differences are repaired by copy rule, or tombstoned and deleted if missing.
haiku-low.q10: Both directions pass through the paused state, which returns 503, and every instance must report paused. In-flight writes finish after 10 s. Abort at 55 s or if the outbox is not drained by 50 s, setting mysql.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns new ids after the switch. setval uses GREATEST(last_value, auto_inc + 1000000), so re-switching after rollback keeps the counter above used ids. MySQL's counter advances from explicit mirror inserts.
haiku-low.q12: Postgres writes are mirrored to MySQL via the outbox and copy rule. Rollback: pause, drain Postgres outbox, check max(id), set mysql. The option ends when 7.1 sets postgres_only.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first (one transaction changing users and inserting an outbox row), then after commit the row is copied to Postgres inline (200 ms timeout, circuit breaker). A Postgres error never fails the request; the caller sees success.
sonnet.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the existing row's version (and no tombstone exists for the id). Missing rows are inserted.
sonnet.q3: app_flag_value{flag="users_write_state"} must read mysql on every web and worker instance for at least 60 seconds, outbox rows are being created, and pg_apply_failures_total is not climbing (step 1.2 passes); the operator then sets users_backfill_enabled. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change (30 s refresh).
sonnet.q4: It reads from the replica (not the primary), in batches of at most 2,000 rows, and checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds before each read: if the metric is missing or above 5 s it sleeps 2 s and checks again without reading. Only one backfill runs at a time.
sonnet.q5: Reads to Postgres: the latest compare pass (2.1) is clean and finished within the last 24 hours (2.1 starts after backfill is done and oldest outbox row is under 1 minute); then ramp 1%, 10%, 50%, 100%, about an hour each. Source-of-truth move (gate for 4.1): reads at 100% on Postgres for at least 72 hours since pg_reads_full_since, last clean compare pass within 24 hours, no fallback rate above 0.1% or confirmed mismatches resetting the clock.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row, inserted in the same MySQL transaction as the change, records it; it is kept in the MySQL users_outbox table. The repair worker (using exponential backoff capped at 5 minutes, reading the current row from the MySQL primary and applying the copy rule to Postgres, then deleting the outbox row) brings Postgres back in line.
sonnet.q7: The copy rule: under the per-user lock, if a tombstone exists for the id the copy skips the user. The erasure job writes a tombstone in the same transaction as the hard delete, and repair writes a tombstone if the row is gone. However, the Open questions admit a window remains: a replica read before erasure can insert into Postgres before the delete reaches it (repair removes it later); not closed yet.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres table users_migration_state (last_id, lease owner, lease expiry). Each batch's rows and the last_id checkpoint commit in one Postgres transaction (checkpoint set only if lease_owner is still this worker), so no batch is half applied. It stops when a batch read comes back empty, then marks the backfill done.
sonnet.q9: Full compare passes (2.1; also daily during holds, and Postgres-to-MySQL passes in 5.3) scan the replica and Postgres together in id order in batches of 2,000 with the lag pause, comparing (id, email, name, plan, version, updated_at) and flagging ids only in Postgres. Each mismatch is re-read from the MySQL primary after a short wait; only persisting differences are confirmed. Confirmed ones are repaired with the copy rule; if the primary no longer has the row, a tombstone is written and the Postgres row deleted. A pass is clean with zero confirmed mismatches; a mismatch remaining after repair stops cutover for investigation.
sonnet.q10: Every change between mysql and postgres goes through the paused state: writes return retryable 503 (Retry-After: 1) until every instance reports paused (up to ~30 s, abort if not by 35 s), then 10 s wait plus 5-second transaction timeouts let in-flight writes end, then outbox drains, setval and checks, then flip to postgres. Budget is 90 s max pause; aim to flip by about 50 s. If it runs long (outbox not empty at 50 s, setval/check fails, or no flip by 55 s), abort by setting users_write_state back to mysql; instances resume within ~30 s, pause ends by ~85 s at worst, with no data lost.
sonnet.q11: Postgres, via its identity sequence (INSERT ... RETURNING id). Before the switch, while writes are paused, the counter is set with setval to GREATEST(last_value, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT + 1,000,000), so it is above MySQL's ids with a margin. While MySQL is a mirror, explicit inserts push its counter forward, so it stays safe. After a rollback, re-running Phase 4 uses GREATEST(...) so the counter stays above every id already used.
sonnet.q12: Postgres is source of truth and each write is copied to MySQL inline via the copy rule (MySQL uses GET_LOCK and a version check), with the Postgres outbox and mirror repair worker retrying failures (alerts on age); daily Postgres-to-MySQL compare passes keep it complete. Rollback (Phase 6): pause writes, wait for all instances to report paused, let in-flight finish, drain Postgres outbox into MySQL, check max(id) matches, flip users_write_state to mysql (aborting back to postgres on any failure); run a mirror compare pass before. Within the same 90 s budget. The option ends at 7.1 when users_write_state is set to postgres_only (after 14+ days, gates met, owner sign-off), which freezes MySQL: point of no return.
